text.vous: Address the reader formally with "vous" (imperative and verbs in the second person plural), as is the norm in France. Never use "tu".

style.loanwords_text: Translate technical terms when a natural French word exists (portefeuille, jeton, contrat intelligent); keep English only for the terms the terminology list keeps (blockchain, pool, staking, exchange, on-chain). The terminology list below wins over this rule.
writing_rules: Use sentence case in headings, titles and menu labels, not English Title Case (« Clés de dépense et adresses », not « Clés De Dépense Et Adresses »).
Use « » for quotations, with a space inside the marks: « exemple ».
Make adjectives and participles agree with the noun in gender and number (une adresse transparente, des transactions protégées).
Abbreviations take a full stop only when the last letter of the word is dropped (M., p. ex., etc.), not when it is kept (Mme, Dr) and never on symbols or acronyms (ZEC, ZIP, km).
English terms kept in English take the French article and the plural -s where usual in French (un exchange, des exchanges, les pools).
Never put English in brackets inside a Markdown link label.

shielded.context: Zcash privacy sense: une adresse protégée, une transaction protégée, les pools protégés. Agree with the noun.

node.inflection: It is NOT a loanword: use the translated term in compounds and plurals too.

transparent.inflection: Agree with the noun: un pool transparent, une adresse transparente, des transactions transparentes.
transparent.notes: Dwarf + Laboré: transparent / transparente, agreeing with the noun.

exchange.context: a trading platform (un exchange, les exchanges); the verb and a generic swap are échange / échanger

viewing-key.context: Exception: the protocol names written with capitals in the English (Viewing Key, Full Viewing Key, Incoming Viewing Key) stay in English exactly as written: la Full Viewing Key.
viewing-key.notes: This would be the best translation. I assume that most french will understand the english word as well.

swap.context: exchanging one coin for another (un échange); the platform is un exchange

custodial.context: dépositaire = a third party holds your keys (un exchange dépositaire); non-custodial = non dépositaire

zero-knowledge.context: zero-knowledge proof = preuve à divulgation nulle de connaissance (the established French term); as an adjective: une cryptographie à divulgation nulle de connaissance. Product and protocol names containing the words stay as written.
zero-knowledge.notes: Dwarf 2026-11-08: divulgation nulle de connaissance (common usage); Laboré: à connaissance nulle. Gianni: 'preuve à divulgation nulle de connaissance' (the established French term).

turnstile.context: Zcash's accounting check that the coins leaving a pool never exceed what entered it
turnstile.notes: Zcash turnstile is like an accounting audit. So 'sas comptable' would be a wise translation of this mechanism

chain.context: a chain of blocks or a network (la chaîne principale, une autre chaîne). The compounds blockchain and on-chain stay in English; cross-chain is inter-chaînes.

faucet.notes: Dwarf: keep English; Laboré: faucet OK.

use-case.context: a concrete way people use Zcash; menu labels use Cas d'utilisation too
use-case.notes: Dwarf: cas d'usage; Laboré 2026-11-14: cas d'utilisation, 'cas d'usage' is an anglicism. Gianni: second reviewer.

top-up.notes: 'recharge' for the noun, 'recharger' for the verb

commitment.context: the cryptographic value that binds to hidden data (un engagement de note), not a promise
commitment.notes: Dwarf 2026-11-13: engagement (cryptographic sense, not a promise); Laboré OK.

note.context: a Zcash note is a shielded unit of value held by a shielded address (une note protégée); not a remark. Translate 'to note' and a written note normally.
note.notes: Dwarf 2026-11-13: keep English, 'remarque' is the wrong sense; Laboré: note OK.

staking.context: keep English, written as is (le staking)

finalizer.context: a participant in Zcash's proof-of-stake layer that votes to make blocks final; not a sports finalist
finalizer.notes: In French, "finaliste" refers to athletes or teams who participate in the last match of a tournament

bond.context: stake locked and delegated to a finalizer for a period: a locked guarantee (la caution). Not a deposit on an exchange (dépôt) and not a financial bond (obligation). Unbonding = libérer la caution.
bond.notes: Dwarf 2026-11-13: dépôt; Laboré 2026-11-14: caution, because dépôt reads as a plain deposit and this is a locked guarantee. Gianni: second reviewer.

decentralized.inflection: Agree with the noun: un réseau décentralisé, la finance décentralisée.
decentralized.notes: Dwarf: masculine by default, agree with a feminine noun; Laboré OK.

on-chain.context: keep English, written as is (des données on-chain); chain alone is chaîne

smart-contract.notes: Dwarf 2026-11-08: singular contrat intelligent; Laboré OK.

changelog.summary: Imported from the runner's hand-written prompt_head_fr.txt: language variety, loanword rule and the node rendering, approved by the steward as legacy prompt-head rules.

Native review by Dwarf (@DurinDwarf): glossary (62 terms) and menus, with his DM answers of 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-13; second native check by Laboré (@starlabman) on 19 terms, 2026-11-14. Second reviewer adopted for bond (caution) and use case (cas d'utilisation); zero-knowledge = preuve à divulgation nulle de connaissance (steward decision between the two reviewers). Formal vous, « » quotes, decimal comma. Steward alignments: Shielded Pools = Pools protégés and the two zero-knowledge menu labels follow the glossary; Akash Network stays a brand name.
